base.description: The 4 LFF chassis, 878972-B21, with every drive bay and the optical bay blanked, both riser cages with their slots blanked, the media module and serial port blanked, one 500 W Flex Slot supply in PS 1 and the blank in PS 2. THIS IS THE BUILD THE PHOTOGRAPHS SHOW, NOT WHAT THE PART NUMBER SHIPS WITH: the QuickSpecs gives the configure-to-order chassis no riser as standard (a primary riser blank, which is not drawn) and makes the supply a choice; one 500 W supply is what the pre-configured models carry, and the secondary riser is an option that needs processor 2.

lff4.description: The 4 LFF CTO server, 878972-B21, as photographed: LFF low-profile drives in bays 1 and 2, blanks in 3 and 4, the optical blank, one 500 W Flex Slot supply in PS 1 and the blank in PS 2, all three PCIe slots blanked.

lff4-options.description: The 4 LFF server with its rear options fitted, to show what the openings take: a full-height card in slot 1 and low-profile cards in slots 2 and 3 (three of the library's ConnectX cards, chosen because their ports show whether a window is in the right place - not an HPE-qualified build), the 1GbE Media Module adapter (NIC ports 3 and 4), the serial port, and a second 500 W supply in PS 2 (which needs the redundant power supply enablement kit; HPE does not support mixing two different supplies).

sff8.description: The 8 SFF chassis, 878973-B21, with the media bay blank and every bay blanked; one 500 W Flex Slot supply in PS 1 and both riser cages, as the base configuration and with the same caveat - the configure-to-order chassis ships with no riser and a chosen supply.

sff8-drives.description: The 8 SFF CTO server, 878973-B21, as HPE's product image shows it: a SmartCarrier drive in each of the eight bays and the media bay blank.

datasheet.title: QuickSpecs HPE ProLiant DL160 Gen10 Server

description: HPE's 1U two-socket Intel Xeon Scalable rack server of the Gen10 generation, in its two front builds - four 3.5 inch LFF bays (878972-B21) or eight 2.5 inch SFF bays with a media bay (878973-B21) - over one rear: three PCIe 3.0 slots on two risers, two Flex Slot power supply bays, two embedded 1GbE ports, the iLO 5 port, VGA, two USB 3.0 ports, and blanks for the media module and the optional serial port. Retired by HPE; the QuickSpecs carries HPE's RETIRED notice.

gaps.note: no system power figure in the QuickSpecs (four editions), User Guide or Maintenance and Service Guide; each gives per-supply ratings and defers to HPE Power Advisor, a web tool, for configured draw. ENERGY STAR's certified server list has no DL160 Gen10 entry and the SPECpower result a search attributes to it is a DL360 Gen10. The server profile's power requirement is unmet for that reason.
gaps.wanted: a configured power figure from HPE (Power Advisor output or a DL160 Gen10 power specification)

gaps.note: the 8 SFF media bay accepts the optical drive cage (873961-B21 enablement kit, 9.5 mm drives 726536-B21 / 726537-B21) or the two-bay SFF drive cage (866458-B21), and the 4 LFF optical bay the 9.5 mm drive; only the blanks are drawn. The User Guide elevations GUID-696364B2 and GUID-7FDCEC9A show both options at 1.36 px/mm; the only photograph of either is a reseller's 10 SFF unit from above, and of the optical kit only its bare bracket and cables.
gaps.wanted: straight-on images of the optical drive bezel and the two-bay SFF cage in a DL160 Gen10

gaps.note: three Flex Slot supplies the QuickSpecs lists are not drawn: 865438-B21 (800 W Titanium), 865428-B21 (800 W Universal, HVAC/HVDC) and 865434-B21 (800 W -48 VDC). The Flex Slot QuickSpecs gives the DC supplies a different length (18.29 cm) and no image of any of the three faces is held.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of each supply's face

gaps.note: the server also exists with a non-hot-plug supply in place of the two Flex Slot bays: the User Guide's enablement procedure begins "Remove the non-hot-plug power supply" before fitting the redundant power supply cage, the system board has a non-hot-plug power supply connector, the Parts Support Guide heads a section with it, and HPE's own rear product image (straight on) shows one wide plate with a fan marked 92% and a single inlet where the bays are. No document held names its part number or rating or says which models shipped with it - every model in QuickSpecs versions 6 to 32 is listed with a hot-plug supply - so that rear is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: the non-hot-plug supply's part number and rating, and which models carried it

gaps.note: no image held shows a card in any of the three PCIe slots; which way up each bracket lies follows from where the riser connectors are, which HPE's PartSurfer photograph shows for the primary riser and only the User Guide's board figure for the secondary (see the riser parts). Not drawn: the FlexibleLOM riser (primary riser board x8/FlexibleLOM, 878539-001, kit 875748-B21) and the FlexibleLOM adapters it carries - PartSurfer photographs the cage at an angle, labelled 'Slot 2 PCIe x8 / Slot 1 ALOM x8', which shows what it is and not the size of its rear opening - and the primary riser BLANK (878532-001) a server ordered with no riser carries, which PartSurfer photographs straight on. The three Media Module adapters are drawn from PartSurfer's photographs, each centred in the opening because no image shows one fitted.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on rear image of a server with the FlexibleLOM riser and an adapter fitted, and of one with a card in each slot and a Media Module adapter fitted

gaps.note: the top view is drawn from the QuickSpecs Internal View, a photograph that fails the panel gate at 3.6%, so every interior position is a fraction and is estimated; and it is the only top-down image held. Not drawn because no image shows them from above: the redundant power supply cage and its power distribution board (the photograph has the non-hot-plug supply), the secondary riser cage for slot 3 (not fitted in the photograph), the drive cage and backplane under the lid, the energy pack, and the 4 LFF chassis' interior.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned plan of the DL160 Gen10 interior, or HPE's service model

gaps.note: the front bezel option is not drawn: the QuickSpecs lists the HPE 1U Gen10 Bezel Kit 867998-B21, which needs the quick-release ear kit, and the User Guide has 'Installing the front bezel option'. The only image held of it is a reseller's angled photograph.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on image of the 1U Gen10 bezel on a DL160 Gen10

gaps.note: the interior is drawn fully populated, as the QuickSpecs photographs it. A one- processor server carries fan blanks in bays 1 to 4 (User Guide, Fan population guidelines) and a cover on processor socket 2; neither part is drawn, so every configuration shows two heatsinks and seven fans.
gaps.wanted: images of the fan blank and of the empty processor 2 socket

attrs.redundancy-note: User Guide, Fan mode behavior and Fan population guidelines: the redundant fan kit adds one fan, and in redundant fan mode one fan rotor failure switches the system to non-redundant mode and it continues to operate; a second failure or a missing fan causes an orderly shutdown

fans.description: the seven single-rotor fan bays, numbered from the power supply side as the User Guide numbers them

interior.description: the system board and the primary riser cage

memory.description: the sixteen DDR4 slots, eight per processor, numbered here 1 to 16 left to right as seen from above with the rear at the top: 1 to 8 are processor 2 slots 1 to 8 and 9 to 16 are processor 1 slots 1 to 8, which is how the QuickSpecs memory population figure numbers them

processors.description: the two processor heatsinks - processor 1 on the right as the front faces you

attrs.redundancy-note: QuickSpecs: the pre-configured models carry one 500 W Flex Slot supply and are RPS ready; the Redundant Power Supply Enablement Kit 866442-B21 is required with a Flex Slot supply on a configure-to-order chassis, and the User Guide calls the second supply the redundant one - the same capacity twice, not twice the capacity

risers.description: the primary riser cage (PCIe slots 1 and 2) and the secondary (slot 3, with processor 2); the slots are bays of the risers

usb.description: the USB Type-A ports front and rear, the front iLO service port among them

name: dl160-gen10

chassis.note: QuickSpecs page 32 and the User Guide's mechanical specifications agree: 4.29 x 43.46 x 61.49 cm (the User Guide prints the depth 61.50), 1U. 434.6 is the body between the ear folds, which is how both front and rear photographs measure (below), so the 43.46 cm is the body, not the rack face. Neither document says what the depth runs between - whether it takes in the ears or the PSU handles.

controls.note: User Guide "Front panel LEDs and buttons": UID button/LED (solid blue activated; flashing blue remote management, firmware upgrade or iLO reboot), NIC status LED (solid green linked; flashing green active; off none), Health LED (solid green normal; flashing green iLO rebooting; flashing amber degraded; flashing red critical), Power On/Standby button and system power LED (solid green on; flashing green power-on sequence; solid amber standby; off no power). The same four on both fronts. Rear: NIC link and status on each RJ45, UID, and each supply's lamp ("Rear panel LEDs").

dimm-numbering.note: QuickSpecs page 31, 'Memory Population guidelines': a figure captioned 'HPE DL160/DL180 Gen 10 Servers Front Server (2+1+1 slots per channel)' draws the P2 CPU on the left and the P1 CPU on the right, each with slots numbered 1 2 3 4 one side of its socket and 5 6 7 8 the other, left to right, and the table under it gives the population order. The plan's dimm-1..8 are therefore processor 2 slots 1..8 and dimm-9..16 processor 1 slots 1..8; the User Guide's System board components figure agrees on which processor is which. A FIRST VERSION RECORDED THIS AS A GAP, 'stated in no document held': the figure is a picture, the text conversion dropped it, and a search of the converted text found only the table.

drive-numbering.note: User Guide "Drive bay numbering": 4 LFF numbered 1..4 left to right; 8 SFF 1..6 in columns of two, top to bottom, then 7 and 8 under the media bay. The 4 LFF front prints each number with a down-pointing triangle on the strip above its bay - at 11.0, 143.8, 281.6 and 388.0, which is where the photograph puts them, not over each bay's centre. The 8 SFF image prints no bay numerals on the strip or the carriers at 2.18 px/mm - and the same image resolves the 1.5 mm legends of the control column, so that is a reading and not a limit of the picture - so none are printed here.

ears.note: THE EARS ARE NOT DRAWN. On the front photograph the ears run 8..71 and 1206..1270 px with the body between the fold gaps at 72.5 and 1204.5 px: 1263 px ear to ear is 484.9 mm at the body's scale, 25 mm an ear. The left ear carries only a thumbscrew; the right ear the HPE element, a thumbscrew and a "ProLiant DL160 Gen10" model label. The control cluster sits on the body, not the ears, which is what decides it (the Dell R660 draws its ears because its control panels are on them). The HPE element is a logo and would not be drawn anyway.

environmental.note: QuickSpecs pages 32-33 and the User Guide's environmental table: operating 10 to 35 C at sea level, derated 1 C per 305 m to 3050 m; extended 5..10 and 35..40 C, and 40..45 C, for approved configurations only (document a00026969en_us); non- operating -30 to 60 C; operating humidity 8 to 90% non-condensing, 28 C maximum wet bulb; altitude 3050 m operating, 9144 m non-operating; acoustics LWAd 4.5 B idle and 5.1 B operating for both builds.

faces.note: Bottom, left and right are sized from the QuickSpecs dimensions and declared empty: no document held shows the base or the sides straight on.

front-lff.note: Four LFF bays, 108.65 apart, each seating a 104.8 x 27.5 carrier at 1.73 into its bay and 13.8 down. Above them the top strip, 0..12.7: the optical drive blank across bays 1 and 2 (a separate plate - its seam is at 455 px), chassis vents from 149.0 to 277.5 in two rows of 5.0 slots on a 6.37 pitch, the information pull tab at 289.7..326.9, two more vent columns at 327.6, the iLO service port in a printed dashed box centred at (349.6, 7.9), the USB 3.0 port at (369.6, 7.4), two vent columns at 381.6, then the UID button (401.0, 6.6), NIC status lamp (409.4, 6.8), Health lamp (417.1, 6.8) and Power button (425.6, 6.6), each with its legend above it. A bright lip runs along the bottom, 41.2..42.9.

front-sff.note: Eight SFF bays as the User Guide numbers them - columns of two, 1 over 2, 3 over 4, 5 over 6 - with the media bay over columns 4 and 5 and bays 7 and 8 beneath it. Columns start at 5.3 on an 81.75 pitch (the rails at 73, 248, 427, 606 and 786 px); rows at 6.8 and 24.5; each carrier 76.2 x 15.0. The media bay blank runs 245.5..408.6 from 0.7 down to 22.8. The top strip, 0..5.8, carries a row of slots and, over column 3, the slim information pull tab at 188.1..221.6. The control column, 409..434.6, stacks the Power button at (416.4, 9.0), the Health lamp (416.4, 17.3), the NIC lamp (416.4, 25.4) and the UID button (416.4, 33.4), each under its printed mark, beside the USB 3.0 port (426.0, 12.0) and the iLO service port (426.3, 30.9) in its printed dashed box, both USB Type-A turned upright. The order top to bottom agrees with the User Guide close-up (native figure GUID-812F8899, callouts 4, 3, 2, 1).

gate-1-front.note: The 4 LFF front photograph passes the panel gate. The body between the ear folds is 1132 px for the 434.6 mm width, 2.6047 px/mm across, and 112.2 px top to bottom for the 42.9 mm height, 2.615 px/mm down - 0.4% apart, so the face is near-orthographic. Every front 4 LFF position is read off it at those scales. The bay pitch is a check: the four bays divide the body at 73, 354, 637 and 920 px, an even 282.3 px against the 282.75 that 434.6 / 4 gives.

gate-1-rear.note: The rear photograph passes the panel gate, less comfortably: the body is 1261 px across for 434.6 (2.90 px/mm) and 123 px down for 42.9 (2.87), 1.2% apart. Every rear position is read off it at those scales, to about a millimetre. The photograph is cropped tight at both sides; the body's edges are at 9 and 1270 px.

gate-1-sff.note: The 8 SFF front is measured off HPE's straight-on product image of that face, as hosted by Express Computer Systems (expresscomputersystems.com/cdn/shop/files/dl 160-gen10-drive-8sff_1835d8c9-1c70-466f-aed1-349e0d74a3b8.jpg, 1080 x 1080), found in a third web search after the first two had found none. It passes the panel gate: the body between the ear folds is 946 px for 434.6 mm (2.177 px/mm) and 93 px for 42.9 (2.168), 0.4% apart, and ear to ear it is 484.9 mm, the 4 LFF photograph's figure. THIS VIEW WAS FIRST DRAWN FROM THE USER GUIDE'S LINE ELEVATIONS (native figures GUID-7FDCEC9A, GUID-55DF0433), which fail the gate at 6% vertical stretch; against the image they had the column pitch right (81.4 against 81.75) and three things wrong - the carrier 3.7 mm too wide, the media bay blank one drive row tall where it runs to the top of the face, and the SmartCarrier's handle on the wrong side of its ring.

interior.note: THE TOP VIEW IS DRAWN FROM ONE PHOTOGRAPH THAT FAILS THE PANEL GATE. The QuickSpecs' Internal View (a00021860enw page 3; the version 6 edition embeds it at 1171 x 728) photographs the 8 SFF server from above with its lid off. Turned so the rear is at the top - the plan's orientation, x as the front view has it - the chassis is 576.5 px across for 434.6 mm (1.3265 px/mm) and 845 px down for 614.9 (1.374), 3.6% apart: a camera above a box, with perspective. Every position is therefore a fraction on its own axis and is estimated; what the photograph gives well is arrangement and count. Two checks on it: a DIMM socket with its latches measures 197 px, 143 mm at the down scale, for a 133.35 mm module; and the primary riser cage starts at 308 mm where the rear photograph, a different image, puts slot 1's window at 309.4.

interior-layout.note: From the photograph and HPE's two figures. The User Guide's System board components figure (native figure GUID-944C6994, rear at the top) puts processor 2 on the left and processor 1 on the right, eight DIMM slots to each - four either side of its socket - and fan connectors 1 to 7 along the front edge from the left; its Fan locations figure (GUID-4CD08C59) numbers the fan bays 1 to 7 from the supply's side. On the photograph: sixteen DIMM slots on a 9.45 pitch in banks of four, eight and four starting at 85.2, 213.9 and 379.4 (centres; latches found by a pixel profile along both ends of the sockets), 236.4 from the rear; the two heatsinks between the banks; seven fans, 404 from the rear, DRAWN ON ONE PITCH WITH ONE BREAK: fans 1 to 4 and fans 5 to 7 on 47.8, and 52.8 between fans 4 and 5, where the photograph shows a bracket in the fan row. That is a fit, and this is what it was fitted to: the fans' labels sit at 105.5, 151.9, 198.3, 247.3, 300.0, 347.2 and 397.3 on the photograph (steps 46.4, 46.4, 49.0, 52.7, 47.2, 50.1), and the Fan locations figure, an independent drawing, steps its seven boxes 45.6, 45.6, 47.8, 53.4, 45.6 and 51.1. Both are widest between 4 and 5; the other steps differ by 2 to 5 mm in images where a pixel is 0.75 and 1.1 mm and a label sits within two pixels of its fan's middle. The fitted centres - 104.0, 151.8, 199.6, 247.4, 300.2, 348.0, 395.8 - are within 1.5 mm of every measured one, which is inside what either image can resolve, so the scatter is recorded here and not drawn; the primary riser cage at the rear right. The supplies are placed from the rear view's bays, not from the photograph, which shows the non-hot-plug supply.

interior-population.note: DRAWN AS THE QUICKSPECS PHOTOGRAPHS IT: two processors, sixteen DIMMs, seven fans ("2 CPUs - 6 standard fans (1 redundant fan shown)", "Fully populated 16 DIMMs shown"). The User Guide's Fan population guidelines give the other builds - one processor non-redundant: fans in bays 5, 6 and 7 and blanks in 1 to 4; one processor redundant: bay 3 as well; two processors non-redundant: bays 2 to 7. The fan blank and the empty processor socket are not drawn, so the configurations here do not vary the interior; see the gap.

lifecycle.note: HPE's own QuickSpecs a00021860enw opens with "RETIRED: This document has been officially retired, and the base products listed herein are now considered obsolete and are no longer available for sale", and buy.hpe.com no longer lists the product. That retired QuickSpecs is the vendor document cited. Third-party EOL trackers (Park Place, eosl.date, Techbuyer) give 31 October 2024 as the last order date for Gen10 and October 2029 for end of support; no HPE notice stating those dates was found, so they are not written as dates.

power.note: NO SYSTEM POWER FIGURE IS STATED in the QuickSpecs (current edition and versions 6, 10 and 14), the User Guide or the Maintenance and Service Guide: each gives per-supply ratings and the 500 W supply's maximum input (557 W at 100 VAC) and points at HPE's Power Advisor for configured draw. Searched outside them too: ENERGY STAR's certified enterprise servers list (data.energystar.gov dataset qifb-fcj2) returns 70 ProLiant entries, DL360 and DL380 Gen10 among them, and no DL160 Gen10; the one SPECpower result a search attributes to this server (power_ssj2008-20190312-00916) is a DL360 Gen10; and the "55 W idle, 380 W maximum" that search summaries repeat traces to a hobbyist calculator, not to HPE. A supply's input rating is not the server's draw, so no power-max is written and the gap stays open.

psus.note: QuickSpecs: the pre-configured models carry "1x 500W Hot Plug; RPS ready"; on the configure-to-order chassis (878972-B21, 878973-B21) the supply is a choice of one or two, and the DL160/180 Gen10 Redundant Power Supply Enablement Kit 866442-B21 is "required with selection of power supply". Whether that means any Flex Slot supply or only a second one the QuickSpecs does not say; the User Guide fits the kit by first removing the non-hot-plug supply, which reads as any. Supplies offered: 865408-B21 500 W Platinum, 865414-B21 800 W Platinum, 865438-B21 800 W Titanium, 865428-B21 800 W Universal (HVAC/HVDC), 865434-B21 800 W -48 VDC. The 500 W and the 800 W Platinum are drawn (hpe/psu-865408-b21@1, hpe/psu-865414-b21@1); the other three are a gap. The bays are the supply's 68.0 x 40.4, from HPE's QuickSpecs HPE Flexible Slot Power Supplies (c04346217), which the rear photograph had measured at 68.2 x 40.6. The default seats the 500 W in PS 1 and the blank in PS 2, as photographed. A NON-HOT-PLUG SUPPLY ALSO EXISTS and is not drawn - see the gap.

rear.note: From the rear photograph, left to right along the top: the primary riser cage (0..203.0) with slot 1's full-height window (15.9..125.2) and slot 2's low- profile window (127.9..188.2), then the secondary riser cage (203.0..285.5) with slot 3's window (214.8..275.1, its vents level with slot 2's). Along the bottom: two screw holes, the media module opening (13.6..58.6), the stacked USB 3.0 ports in a dark bezel (59.0..79.0), the iLO RJ45 with its legend turned on its side, VGA in a blue field (103.8..136.9), NIC 1 and 2 in a pale bezel (138.6..173.8), a vent block, the UID lamp (195.9, 35.5), a small round hole, and under slot 3 the IOIOI legend and the serial port blank. The two supply bays fill the right end, PS 2 at 286.9 and PS 1 at 362.4, with the PS 1 / PS 2 legend printed upright on the strip between them, PS over the digit over an arrow.

rear-numbering.note: User Guide "Rear panel components": 1 PCIe slot 1 or FlexibleLOM adapter (optional), 2 PCIe slot 2, 3 PCIe slot 3 (secondary riser for processor 2, optional), 4 Flexible Slot power supply 2 (hot-plug, optional), 5 Flexible Slot power supply 1 (hot-plug), 6 Serial port (optional), 7 NIC ports 1-2 (1Gb), 8 VGA port, 9 iLO Management Port, 10 USB 3.0 ports, 11 Media Module adapter (optional NIC ports 3-4). The photograph's printed legends agree: PS 1 points right and PS 2 left, and the media module window is printed 3 and 4.

slots.note: User Guide "PCIe expansion slot definitions": slot 1 PCIe 3.0 x16, full-height half-length or low-profile, or a FlexibleLOM (x8); slot 2 PCIe 3.0 x8 low- profile; slot 3 PCIe 3.0 x16 low-profile, on the secondary riser with processor 2. THE SLOTS ARE BAYS OF THE RISERS, each a standard bracket behind a window in its cage (hpe/riser-primary-dl160@1, hpe/riser-secondary-dl160@1), so the library's generic cards and its card families seat in them. They were first drawn as chassis bays the size of the windows the photograph shows - 109.3 x 23.3 and 60.3 x 18.2 - and nothing but HPE's blanks fitted; the same was true of the media module and serial openings, which are now the openings' own sizes and accept the Media Module adapter and the serial port. The photographed unit has blanks in all five.

sources.note: Read for this model: QuickSpecs a00021860enw (retired edition, Aug 2025), HPE's datasheet for the model, for dimensions, weights, chassis builds, options and environmentals; User Guide a00066666en_us ed. 7, the server's hardware guide, for component identification, LEDs, drive and slot numbering and specifications, both as its PDF export and as the HTML zip whose native figures (GUID-*-high.png, 675 px) are the line drawings cited below; Maintenance and Service Guide a00066664en_us, the service manual; two straight-on photographs from newserverlife's hands-on review - the 4 LFF front (newserverlife.com/upload/iblock/562/7_opt.jpeg, 1280 x 131) and the rear (.../386/8_opt.jpeg, 1280 x 145). No vendor 3D model exists for this server on any page searched, and NetBox's devicetype-library has no DL160 Gen10.

weight.note: QuickSpecs page 32 by configuration: SFF minimum 10.97 kg (1 drive, 1 DIMM, 3 fans, 1 processor, 1 supply), SFF maximum 13.92, LFF minimum 11.65, LFF maximum 15.74. The User Guide's mechanical table rounds to 10.00 minimum and 16.00 maximum "approximate values"; the QuickSpecs figures are the configured ones and are carried.
